content.title: Sebastian Fundora knocks out Keith Thurman; fight card results, highlights
content.text: March 28, 2026Updated March 30, 2026, 12:56 p.m. CTSebastian Fundora defeated Keith Thurman by TKO in the sixth round, defending his WBC junior middleweight title.The victory marked Fundora's third straight stoppage and Thurman's second career loss.Sebastian Fundora became the first man to stop Keith Thurman on March 28 in Las Vegas, successfully defending his WBC junior middleweight title with a sixth-round TKO of the 37-year-old former unified world champion.It was Fundora's third defense of his WBC belt, further solidifying his claim for divisional supremacy as he scores a third straight stoppage. Thurman suffers his second career loss and first since a 2019 defeat to Manny Pacquiao."It was a lot easier than I expected," Fundora said in the ring afterwards. "I was a little nervous today because he's such a big name. Again, he's such a big fighter. But we got in there and I reminded myself as soon as we stepped into that ring that this is my world. You're in my world."Fundora utilized his nine-inch height advantage and 11-inch reach advantage to pick Thurman apart from range, working effectively behind the jab in the early rounds before opening up and connecting with frequent combinations as the bout progressed.He nearly dropped Thurman with a quick left hand in the second round and by the fifth Fundora was battering Thurman across the ring, momentum which he carried into the sixth, forcing referee Thomas Taylor to step in and waive the fight off despite protests from Thurman.After the bout Fundora declined to call out his contemporaries, instead stating he's open to any opponent while lauding the talent pool at junior middleweight, widely considered to be one of boxing's deepest divisions."I'll fight whoever," Fundora said. "There are all kinds of names, there are big names. I think 154 (pounds) is the best division right now. Whoever wants it next, we can get it."See below for The Tennessean's live updates from throughout the Fundora vs. Thurman fight card. Sebastian Fundora vs Keith Thurman fight card resultsSebastian Fundora def. Keith Thurman by TKO in Round 6Yoenis Tellez def. Brian Mendoza by unanimous decisionYoenli Hernandez def. Terrell Gausha by TKO in Round 4Gurgen Hovhannisyan def. Cesar Navarro by TKO in Round 5 Sebastian Fundora vs Keith Thurman live updates Sebastian Fundora vs Keith Thurman: Round 6Fundora landed 36 punches in the fifth, more than any other Thurman opponent has landed in a round. Fundora opens aggressively and is backing Thurman up with repeated hooks. Thurman's face is real bloody now as Fundora tees off along the ropes and tags him with a handful of punches. Trying to close the distance Thurman gets cracked with a straight shot and it's only a few more moments before referee Thomas Taylor steps in to stop the bout! Thurman protests but he was getting thoroughly beaten over the last two rounds. Sebastian Fundora vs Keith Thurman: Round 5Thurman opens the round connecting a big right hand, probably his best punch so far. It's not long before Fundora is back to cracking Thurman, landing a big left hand to the chin before continuing the onslaught along the ropes and landing some glancing punches which get the crowd excited. Fundora just misses on a massive hook before landing a few looping shots to the body moments after. Straight left hand lands for Fundora now, as Thurman can't do much more than clinch and move. Fundora tees off the close the round and connects a solid left hand just before the bell. Big round for Fundora. Sebastian Fundora vs Keith Thurman: Round 4Thurman lands an early straight left hand to the head of Fundora, but it's not long after Fundora lands a straight shot of his own which pushes Thurman back. Fundora lands a left uppercut now before following with a right which connects. Midway through the round Fundora begins to stack some hooks forcing Thurman to get on his bike. Fundora hasn't let up the pressure and in the corner again pops Thurman, but Thurman comes back and lands a couple body shots in the center not long after. Fundora largely in control, with Thurman unable to avoid the pressure. Sebastian Fundora vs Keith Thurman: Round 3Fundora chasing Thurman down around the outside of the ring early, but hasn't let much loose outside of the jab. Now Thurman picks his moment to sit down on some punches and connects a right hand clean. Thurman lands a looping punch over the top not long after, but it's just a glancing shot which is taken well by Fundora. Thurman connects to the body now and Fundora comes right back at him, landing some thumping punches in the corner. Sebastian Fundora vs Keith Thurman: Round 2Fundora outlanded Thurman 8-3 in the opening round. Early on, Thurman darts inside and connects to the body before ducking out of range. Just moments later Fundora connects clean and buckles the knees of Thurman, but Thurman recovers before taking further damage. Now Thurman lands to the stomach of Fundora again, but he's only been able to land one punch at a time thus far. Fundora has been pretty methodical working behind the jab, yet to open up and trade with Thurman. Sebastian Fundora vs Keith Thurman: Round 1We're underway as Thurman looks to turn back the clock and upset the reigning WBC champion Fundora. Fundora wastes no time and lands a thumping straight left clean on the chin of Thurman in the opening seconds. Fundora holding the center of the ring, towering over Thurman with a nine-inch height advantage. Thurman has been moving laterally around the outside and in the final minute he jumps into range with a looping right, but it doesn't seem to connect cleanly. Thurman connects again late, but Fundora should claim the round. Yoenis Tellez defeats Brian Mendoza after suffering nose injuryYoenis Tellez continued down the comeback trail as he defeated former world title challenger Brian Mendoza by unanimous decision in the co-main event. The judges scored the bout 98-92, 97-93 and 97-93.Tellez suffered a nose injury in the third round after an accidental clash of heads, which forced a prolonged stoppage before he ultimately continued. The bout would have been ruled a no contest if stopped in the third, but Tellez instead chose to fight on, going on to outbox Mendoza in a competitive affair throughout.It's Tellez's second win since suffering his lone career defeat to former world champion Abass Baraou last August, while Mendoza suffers his third loss in four fights.See round-by-round updates from the bout below.Round 10: Both fighters will want to close the fight well with the cards seemingly up in the air. Mendoza lands a straight shot on the inside before just avoiding a hook in response from Tellez. In the center of the ring, Tellez connects with a combination forcing Mendoza to initiate a clinch. Now Tellez lands a left and Mendoza comes right back with a combination, landing a few glancing shots. Mendoza connects a couple punches late to close out what should be a close one on the cards.Round 9: In the opening seconds they quickly find themselves in the corner trading some solid shots back and forth. Mendoza lands a nice left to the body but Tellez continues barreling forward and lands a right hook through Mendoza's guard. While clinched they each land to the body and coming out of the clinch Tellez lands a pair of big left hands. Inside the final minute now Mendoza connects clean with a left to Tellez's head. Mendoza landed some solid punches down the stretch despite his cut growing worse. It seems to be close on the cards heading into the final round, with Tellez maybe holding a slight edge.Round 8: Mendoza opens the round connecting on a pair of shots to Tellez's head. Tellez steps inside to land a right hand and moments later tries to follow up with the same shot and seemingly bumps heads with Mendoza again, they continue on though with Mendoza now bleeding from the eye. Into the final minute they trade some solid uppercuts to the body. Moments later Tellez cracks Mendoza with a shot to the chin and pops his head back before the bell.Round 7: Mendoza lands a right hand over the top before following with a left to the body early in the round, but Tellez stays in the pocket and takes it well. Tellez able to respond soon after with a solid jab but he took some damage there. Now Tellez lands the uppercut moments before Mendoza connects a hook as they trade shots in the center of the ring. Inside the final minute now, Tellez lands a handful of looping shots as they exchange, but Mendoza response with some solid body shots. Tellez seems to have gotten the best out of most exchanges that round, but there was some good action from both fighters.Round 6: Mendoza backing Tellez up early with some jabs, but Tellez has shown good defense to avoid the best shots. Now Tellez rips a right to the body of Mendoza but takes a body shot right back. Plenty of punches landing on the guards of each fighter as they go back and forth at close range. Tellez goes down the body of Mendoza with another right hand, and as Mendoza responds Tellez lands a left down low. Mendoza now lands a pair of strong shots, knocking Tellez back with a hook moments before the bell.Round 5: The fight has ebbed and flowed so far, with one fighter connecting a combination before eating a combination in response not long after. Tellez has started well though, landing some solid jabs on the front foot early. Tellez seems to have thrown Mendoza off his rhythm with pressure this round and down the stretch connects on a few thumping shots which seemed to make Mendoza uncomfortable. Tellez has reacted well since the nose injury.Round 4: Punches fly early and each man lands a solid shot down to the body. Mendoza fighting well from the outside, working the jab and finding openings down low. Mendoza again goes to the body with a two-punch combination but moments later Tellez snaps his head back with a jab. We're inside the final minute now and Tellez continues to land the jab while taking some glancing shots in response from Mendoza. Tellez closes the round with a solid right hand to the temple of Mendoza.Round 3: Mendoza comes out of the gate and lands a solid uppercut to start the round. 45 seconds into the round we have an accidental head clash which leaves Tellez on his knees grasping his face, forcing a pause in the action. Tellez took a big hit to the nose and is gushing blood now, he'll have five minutes to recover. A stoppage due to injury would lead to a no contest this early in the fight. Tellez is up and seemingly uncomfortable, leaving a pool of blood below where he'd been kneeling, but decides he'll continue with just over two minutes to go. Mendoza able to land some glancing jabs but Tellez remaining cautious now. Tellez goes down to the body and lands late, but it was a quiet finish after the head clash.Round 2: In the first round 13-of-14 landed punches were jabs, and Tellez opens the second once again firing the jab. Mendoza letting his hands loose from the outside now, but mostly range-finding shots thus far. Tellez has a moment along the ropes as he thumps Mendoza with a solid right to the body. Inside the final minute Mendoza pumps the jab with success before glancing a hook of Tellez's head. Tellez follows up with a solid right hand which backs Mendoza up before the final bell.Round 1: We're underway in the co-main event and jabs begin to fly back and forth, but nothing of significance landing in the opening minute. Few punches other than the jab coming from either fighter thus far, and the power punches thrown have largely been off the mark. Warm-up round for both fighters. Yoenli Hernandez wins after questionable stoppageYoenli Hernandez's dominant performance over Terrell Gausha was capped with a questionable stoppage which is sure to draw referee Allen Huggins plenty of criticism.In the midst of a one-sided beating, Hernandez landed a pair of strong right hands to the head of Gausha in the fourth, then in a momentarily pause in the action Huggins stepped in and waived an end to the bout, drawing immediate protests from Gausha.Despite the early stoppage, which was Gausha's first career knockout loss, Hernandez was dominant from start to finish. He showed a diverse arsenal of punches and thumping power as he landed at will throughout. Hernandez improves to 10-0 with nine knockouts and looks to be a real contender in a dry middleweight division.See round-by-round updates from the bout below.Round 4: The fighters trade shots in the center to start, each landing, but the best punches came from Hernandez to the body of Gausha. Hernandez continues to walk him down, knocking him off balance with a pair of right hands. Then curiously the referee steps in and stops the bout, despite Gausha standing upright and seemingly not hurt. He was getting thoroughly beaten, but certainly didn't seem like a stoppage was warranted. It was an impressive performance by Hernandez, but that's not the way it should've ended.Round 3: Hernandez letting combinations loose early and lands a solid uppercut on the inside. Hernandez standing in front of Gausha, unafraid of anything coming his way as he eyes a countershot. Gausha lands a couple left hands and Hernandez lets his hands loose with him, landing a few thumping shots that force Gausha into a clinch. Hernandez closes the round with a couple big right hands over the top.Round 2: Hernandez lands a looping right to the chin of Guasha on the counter in the opening seconds. Gausha hasn't had enough output to keep Hernandez off of him. Hernandez continues to connect his left hand with ease, whether as a jab or hook to the body. He's also done well to hook the right hand around the guard of Gausha too. Hernandez pounds the body of Gausha with the right down the stretch, continuing to dominate with little response from Gausha.Round 1: We're off and Hernandez is wasting no time letting his jab loose. Early on he backs Gausha into the corner and lands a few nice shots to the body. Midway through the round and the jab to the body has been the best weapon for Hernandez thus far. Inside the final minute Hernandez begins throwing some sharp looping shots with each hand, backing up Gausha as shot after shot lands. One-way traffic in the first. Gurgen Hovhannisyan knocks out Cesar NavarroThe Joe Goossen-trained Gurgen Hovhannisyan kept his unbeaten record intact as he stopped Cesar Navarro in the fifth round of the night's pay-per-view opener.The 6-foot-7 Hovhannisyan controlled the bout behind a stiff jab and in the later rounds began putting together combinations with increasing success. In the fifth he backed Navarro into the ropes with a handful of jabs before connecting with flurry of unanswered punches which forced the referee to step in and stop the bout.Hovhannisyan improves to 10-0 with nine knockouts, while Navarro drops to 15-4.See round-by-round updates from the bout below.Round 5: Navarro flashes a combination early but it doesn't do much to back up Hovhannisyan. Now Hovhannisyan backs Navarro into the ropes and unloads a few real strong shots, connecting well to the body. Hovhannisyan beginning to connect more regularly now as he walks Navarro down, letting shots go from range. Hovhannisyan gets caught with an uppercut in the midst of a nice combination. Hovhannisyan now pumping the jab repeatedly to the head of Navarro doing some real damage. He continues the onslaught against the ropes, repeatedly landing with no response and the referee steps in to stop the bout! Hovhannisyan gets his ninth career stoppage!Round 4: Hovhannisyan opens the round with a few straight left hands which glance off the head of Navarro. They trade right hands in the corner now, with Hovhannisyan landing the harder shot from the orthodox stance. Not a ton coming from Hovhannisyan outside of the jab still. Moments later Hovhannisyan finds some success with the jab followed by the straight right. Down the stretch Hovhannisyan lands a nice two-punch combination along the ropes. Another solid round for Hovhannisyan.Round 3: A straight right hand lands for Navarro just seconds into the round and he's able to follow up with another right moments later. Hovhannisyan back to walking Navarro down with the jab, but he's yet to really let his hands go. Now in the center the fighter's trade straight shots back and forth before Hovhannisyan lands a solid right hand to cap off the exchange. Navarro having his moments picking out straight shots, but Hovhannisyan is largely in control.Round 2: Hovhannisyan throwing a handful of left hands early and connects with a hooking shot in the center. Navarro is having real trouble breaking inside Hovhannisyan's reach so far. Navarro does manage to connect in the corner now as he switches into the southpaw stance, before landing a right hook moments later. It's not sustained though as Hovhannisyan continues to back him up with straight shots. Hovhannisyan closes with a combination, ending another relatively slow round.Round 1: We're underway and it's clear Hovhannisyan isn't going to be the quicker man, but he certainly has the size advantage in the ring. There's a quick exchange in the center of the ring a minute in, with each fighter connecting on some glancing shots. Hovhannisyan pumping the jab while Navarro looks for a way inside, but not much action to speak of in the opening three minutes. Hovhannisyan should take the round behind his jab.What time is Sebastian Fundora vs Keith Thurman fight?The PBC on Prime Video pay-per-view card is set to begin at 7 p.m. (CT) on March 28, with ring walks for the main event expected at approximately 10 p.m. (CT). Three preliminary fights will air free on Prime Video beginning at 4:30 p.m. (CT).PPV start: 7 p.m. CTFundora vs. Thurman ring walks: approx. 10 p.m. CTHow to watch Sebastian Fundora vs Keith Thurman fight?The Sebastian Fundora vs. Keith Thurman headlined fight card will air live on Prime Video pay-per-view, while three preliminary fights will stream free on Prime Video ahead of the main card. The pay-per-view is also available through traditional cable and satellite outlets.How to watch: Prime Video PPVSebastian Fundora vs Keith Thurman pay-per-view pricePBC's four-fight card from Las Vegas is available on Prime Video pay-per-view, as well as through traditional cable and satellite outlets, for $74.99.PPV price: $74.99Sebastian Fundora vs Keith Thurman cardSebastian Fundora (23-1-1, 15 KOs) vs. Keith Thurman (31-1, 23 KOs); WBC junior middleweight titleYoenis Tellez (11-1, 8 KOs) vs. Brian Mendoza (23-4, 17 KOs)Yoenli Hernandez (9-0, 8 KOs) vs. Terrell Gausha (24-5-1, 12 KOs)Gurgen Hovhannisyan (9-0, 8 KOs) vs. Cesar Navarro (15-3, 13 KOs)Preliminary fights (free on Prime Video)Elijah Garcia (17-1, 13 KOs) vs. Kevin Newman II (18-3-1, 11 KOs)Kaipo Gallegos (11-0-1, 9 KOs) vs. Julian Gonzalez (16-1-1, 12 KOs)Brayan Gonzalez (4-0, 3 KOs) vs. Brandon Guerrero (7-4)Fundora vs Thurman oddsFundora enters his third title defense as a -380 favorite, while Thurman is a +280 underdog to win the title. The over/under is set at 9.5 rounds.Fundora by KO/TKO: -125Fundora by decision: +255Thurman by KO/TKO: +600Thurman by decision: +600Odds via DraftKings, as of March 28Sebastian Fundora vs Keith Thurman fight locationThe PBC fight card headlined by Sebastian Fundora vs. Keith Thurman is being held at the MGM Grand Garden Arena in Las Vegas.Location: MGM Grand Garden Arena, Las VegasSebastian Fundora recordSebastian Fundora is 23-1-1 with 15 wins by knockout.Fundora is a former unified champion and has held the WBC 154-pound title since defeating Tim Tszyu in their first bout in March 2024. Fundora has since had two successful defenses, first defeating Chordale Booker by stoppage in March 2025 before winning a rematch against Tszyu last July.Fundora is ranked No. 2 at junior middleweight by The Ring and ESPN.How tall is Sebastian Fundora? Height, reachSebastian Fundora stands at 6-foot-5½, making him the tallest current world champion in boxing. Fundora is 28 years old, nine years younger than Thurman, and has an 80-inch reach. Despite his size, Fundora has spent his entire career fighting at junior middleweight (154-pound limit).Keith Thurman recordKeith Thurman is 31-1 with 23 wins by knockout.Thurman has fought just twice in the six years since suffering his lone career defeat to Manny Pacquiao in 2019, most recently ending a three-year layoff as he defeated Brock Jarvis last March. Prior to his loss against Pacquiao, Thurman had reigned as unified welterweight champion.Thurman is ranked No. 5 at junior middleweight by ESPN.How old is Keith Thurman? Age, heightKeith Thurman is 37, nine years older than Fundora, and stands at 5-9½ with a 69-inch reach. After beginning his career fighting at catchweights, Thurman first campaigned at welterweight (147-pound limit) where he remained until making his junior welterweight debut against Jarvis last year.Boxing fights tonightMoses Itauma vs. Jermaine Franklin; 1 p.m. (CT), March 28; DAZNSebastian Fundora vs. Keith Thurman; 7 p.m. (CT), March 28, Prime Video PPVHarrison Campbell covers boxing for The Tennessean and high school sports for The Daily Herald.
